task: Review this fictional administrative appeal in about 60–100 words. Preserve a firm first-person account of the documented missed reply while distinguishing it from an unsupported claim about intent. Suggest a useful remedy without diluting the complaint into an apology or inventing legal rights.
input: You received my request on 7 April 2026 and wrote, "We will reply by 14 April 2026." It is now 15 April and I have received no reply. You deliberately buried the request. Your silence proves that you never intended to answer, and I demand that this be acknowledged.

facts.text: The fictional acknowledgement records receipt of the request on 7 April 2026.
The acknowledgement says exactly: "We will reply by 14 April 2026."
As of 15 April 2026, the sender has received no reply.
The packet provides no evidence of the recipient's intent or internal handling of the request.

forbidden_additions: Deliberate suppression or an intention never to answer treated as established.
An invented internal explanation, response, legal breach, or compensation entitlement.
An altered quotation or a suggestion that no reply date was promised.
preserve: The legitimate, firmly expressed complaint about a documented missed reply.
A distinction between observable events and inferred motives.
A remedy that seeks an answer or explanation without inventing one.
